turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, it’s bridges. If I know I have to cross one and there’s no way around it, I start getting scared right away—before I’m even on it. My heart pounds, my hands get damp on the steering wheel or the armrest, and I get this terrible rush of fear.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient reports immediate anticipatory fear with palpitations and sweaty hands when a bridge crossing becomes unavoidable, before even getting onto the bridge.

turns.doctor_question: Do you get this same rush of fear in other places where it might be hard to get away, like highways, tunnels, or crowded places?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it the same way in those other places. It’s mainly when it’s a bridge that I know I have to cross.

turns.doctor_question: What is it about being on a bridge that scares you most?
turns.patient_response: I know it doesn’t make sense, really. I know cars go over those bridges all day long. But when I see a big high bridge coming up, or even on the map, it feels like it could just drop away underneath us. That’s what scares me most.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes marked fear of high bridges, specifically imagining that the bridge could drop away beneath the car despite recognizing this fear is irrational.

turns.doctor_question: When you’re on a bridge, is the main fear that the bridge itself will collapse?
turns.patient_response: Yes, that’s really it. I know, in my head, that thousands of cars go over those bridges every day. But when I see a high one coming up, or even see it on the map, it just feels like the whole thing could drop away underneath us.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms a marked fear that a high bridge could collapse beneath the vehicle despite recognizing that this is unlikely.

turns.doctor_question: Do you avoid crossing bridges whenever you can?
turns.patient_response: Yes. For more than two years now, I’ve been planning errands and visits so I don’t have to cross bridges. I’ve stopped going to San Juan, and I don’t really do Seattle theater nights anymore because of it. If I absolutely have to cross one, I need to study the route ahead of time, go at the right time, and have someone with me. Even then I’m scared the whole way across.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient describes routinely planning errands and visits to avoid bridges and requiring extensive accommodations when crossing is unavoidable.
symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient reports marked fear specifically related to crossing bridges.
symptom_reasoning.S063: When bridge crossing cannot be avoided, the patient reports being scared throughout the crossing.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had one of these sudden rushes of fear when you were not around a bridge?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I can’t recall that happening out of the blue. It’s usually tied to the bridge, or knowing I’m going to have to cross one.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient states that fear is usually tied to bridges or anticipating crossing one, supporting a specific situational phobic fear.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient indicates that knowing they will have to cross a bridge triggers fear, supporting anticipatory anxiety in response to the phobic situation.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about crossing a bridge, is your fear mainly that the bridge will collapse?
turns.patient_response: Yes. I know it doesn’t make much sense, because so many cars cross them every day. But when I see a high bridge ahead, or even on the map, it feels like it could just give way underneath us.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient endorses fear that a high bridge could give way underneath them, despite recognizing that this fear is not rational.
